velocity-field: Imagine measuring the speed of whatever passes one marked spot. Must you keep tagging the same drop?
Which quantity does each arrow at a position represent?
volume-flow: Compare the wall speed with the speed in the middle. Can just the wall represent the whole cross-section?
Only a small part of the slice may reach the highest speed. How should slower parts be counted?
mass-flow: Write the mass crossing per second as density × volume per second. Which product must balance?
More density means more mass in each unit of volume. Why would that require motion to stop?
viscous-shear: Look for the speed difference above or below the division sign in the shear rule.
Would a larger difference between neighboring layer speeds make them more alike?
parcel-path: After a parcel leaves the starting spot, which reading from the velocity field applies?
Does the parcel instantly jump into the point with the fastest flow?
local-change: Imagine one sensor attached to a mark on the riverbank. Does it keep the same water molecule?
To measure a change per second, must the two readings be taken at different times?
advective-change: A steady river can have a narrow fast section ahead of a wider slow section. What does a passing leaf experience?
Can the same quantity of water pass both a wide and a narrow section at different speeds?
material-derivative: Check the units of pressure against the units of a change in velocity per time.
Imagine the parcel crossing into faster-moving water. Which change is missing from a fixed sensor’s reading?
streamline-direction: What directions would arrows painted along this curve need to follow?
A streamline is drawn from a snapshot. What happens if tomorrow’s arrows differ?
local-vorticity: Compare two nearby arrows on opposite sides of a tiny paddle wheel. Would its spin depend on more than the bend in one path?
A wheel can travel straight while spinning. Which local differences could produce that spin?
mass-storage: If a container still holds positive mass, can the amount nevertheless be getting smaller?
Try writing incoming per second minus outgoing per second. When does that difference have a minus sign?
outward-mass-flux: Imagine enlarging a doorway while the person keeps walking along the wall. How would they get through it?
Separate motion along the patch from motion through its face.
local-mass-balance: Compare the mass flowing out on the right with what flowed in on the left. Which is larger?
Can a region empty while all the departing mass is still accounted for somewhere else?
parcel-density: Keep the same amount of material and change just the denominator in mass ÷ volume.
Is the parcel assumed incompressible here, or does its volume actually change?
incompressible-flow: Imagine carrying a sealed water balloon. Could its contents move without changing their total volume?
Can a fixed volume fit in more than one shape, for instance a short wide shape and a long narrow one?
no-slip: Where is the no-slip rule applied, at every fluid point or at the surface it touches?
Distinguish a rule linking fluid speed to wall speed from a statement about resistance between fluid layers.
shear-gradient: Keep the viscosity fixed and find the sign of the multiplier connecting shear to velocity slope.
If the slope were zero instead, what would the shear rule predict for the same fluid?
kinematic-viscosity: Kinematic viscosity is dynamic viscosity divided by density. Which of these quantities just changed?
Is density in the numerator of that ratio, or below the line?
viscous-spreading-time: Expand the gap-squared factor into two lengths before doubling the gap.
At the same spreading rate, should momentum take longer or less time to travel farther?
couette-profile: Which of the two plates is moving at the position y = h?
Substitute y = h into y/h before multiplying by the upper-plate speed.
pipe-profile: The pressure gradient drives flow in the interior. What rule applies specifically at the stationary wall?
Sketch the parabolic profile starting at the centre. Where do its sides meet the pipe?
poiseuille-flow: Mass need not be created to move more of it per second. How is the flow speed changing?
Which dimensions of the pipe did the question actually change?
pressure-force-density: Draw the pressure pushes from the left and right faces of a tiny cube. How do their sizes compare?
What would select a preferred negative direction if every face had the same pressure?
euler-fluid-equation: Compare the units of speed divided by density with those of acceleration.
If a parcel moves into water flowing at a different speed, will a fixed-location rate notice that part?
hydrostatic-gradient: Sketch the weight of a thin horizontal layer. Which side must give the larger supporting push?
A zero speed means no acceleration. Can two nonzero forces balance?
bernoulli-streamline: Trace the Bernoulli rule along a single streamline. What lets you connect one streamline with another?
Check which assumption connects separate streamlines, rather than setting all fluid speeds to zero.
viscous-curvature: A parcel with mass can have zero net force. What would balance the two viscous pulls?
Compare the stresses acting on opposite faces. What determines their difference?
navier-stokes-balance: Imagine the same pipe with two different inlet speeds. What tells the equation which flow to describe?
Count the time, motion, viscosity and pressure terms. Which cannot be found from pressure alone?
momentum-flow-balance: List every push acting on the fluid volume before separating out the part due to the wall.
Name the body receiving the computed force. How is the force on the wall related?
reynolds-number: A large ratio can have a small nonzero denominator. Does it require viscosity to vanish?
Are a smooth inlet and a disturbed inlet necessarily equivalent at the same speed?
matching-reynolds: Could the same Reynolds number describe both a sphere and a thin flat plate?
Which effect sets the behavior of free-surface waves? Is it captured by a viscosity ratio alone?
mach-number: Low Mach number compares flow speed with sound speed. Which part of that ratio constrains heating?
Does the ratio involving viscosity determine whether heating expands the liquid or gas?
boundary-layer-scale: In the thickness scale, which side of the fraction contains distance traveled along the wall?
Does x occur alone or inside a square root?
wall-flow-reversal: Look at the direction of the wall shear just before and just after the measured point.
Could a zero velocity gradient produce zero shear while viscosity stays positive?
drag-coefficient: Look at which flow conditions appear when you increase speed. Is drag always in the same regime?
Check the units of force divided by density × speed squared × area.
mean-and-fluctuation: Can a regularly oscillating flow keep all its mass while changing its speed?
Would a perfectly repeating, orderly signal also show departures from its average?
fluctuation-size: Try averaging deviations of +1 and −1, then do the same after squaring.
Which calculation changes a negative deviation to a positive contribution? Does the choice of units do that?
reynolds-shear-stress: Averaging each of two fluctuations can give zero. Can the average of their product still carry information?
Check the units and physical origins of viscosity and a momentum flux caused by fluctuating speeds.
